label: Research pool deep dive A (24 Oct 2026)

payload.writeUp: Deep dive A of 24 October 2026: a fresh look at 21 UK companies already in the pool, re-checking from their own sites, Companies House, platform listings and the press whether each is genuinely raising now, closed, or unknown. Access status found: 9 closed, 2 expected, 6 fundraising reported, 4 unknown. Closed raises are kept so the watch list and timeline stay honest; nothing here is presented as open without a source.

candidate.name: 0rCA (formerly Fishy Filaments)
candidate.teaser: Cornish recycler turning end-of-life fishing nets into like-new PA6 nylon with a containerised, deployable recycling system.
candidate.description: Fishy Filaments Limited (Companies House 10849461, incorporated 4 July 2017, sole director Ian Keith Falconer) trades as 0rCA, rebranded to 0rCA Oceans Renewed in 2025. The company recycles nylon fishing nets into PA6 and sells a containerised recycling system ('0rCA in a Container'); the site reports 6,102 kg of nets recovered, 55,680 kg CO2 saved and 14 boats serviced. Its timeline cites a 2017 crowdfund and Cornwall Council BIG2 grant, a 2019 second round, a 2022 global distribution deal with Fillamentum, a 2024 Shared Prosperity Fund grant for the first full-scale prototype and a GB patent granted in 2025. Press reports a Crowdcube campaign that passed its target in August 2024 (over £100,000 from 215+ investors) and a £126,000 SWIG Finance loan in June 2024. Accounts last made up to 31 July 2025. No live round, valuation or SEIS/EIS statement was found on a readable page; Crowdcube was not read.

candidate.teaser: Bristol maker of carbon-storing wallboard (Breathaboard) and lime plasters, licensing a drop-in platform to gypsum manufacturers.
candidate.description: Adaptavate Limited (Companies House 09214364, incorporated 11 Sept 2014) develops Breathaboard, a bio-based carbon-storing plasterboard alternative, and Breathaplasta lime plasters, and now positions itself as a drop-in platform for gypsum manufacturers. UKRI lists six Innovate UK/ISCF grants worth about £2.37m. Pilots with Legal & General and Oxygen Asset Management; Asia launch via The GEAR by Kajima.

Expansion targets Manchester, then Leeds, London and Bristol.
